name: Svātmārāma

tradition.text: in the succession of Matsyendra and Gorakṣa

realization_account.text: He says he knows haṭhavidyā through the grace (prasāda) of Matsyendra, Gorakṣa and the other Siddhas, and offers the 'lamp of haṭha' out of compassion to those lost in the darkness of many doctrines (HYP 1.3–4).
realization_account.label: the tradition's account

summary: Compiler of the Haṭhapradīpikā (c. 1450), who gathered verses from some twenty earlier haṭha and rājayoga texts into a single four-part system taught 'solely for the sake of rājayoga'. He salutes his guru as 'Nātha' (HYP 1.2); the tradition places him in Gorakṣa's line. Nothing reliable is known of his life.
notes: HYP 1.2 'praṇamya śrīguruṃ nātham' — whether 'Nātha' names a specific guru is not settled.

name: Gheraṇḍa
summary: The sage who, in his hut, teaches Caṇḍakāpāli the sevenfold 'yoga of the pot' in the Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā (c. 1700). The text presents him as a Vaiṣṇava-leaning yogin; no historical information exists.

name: Caṇḍakāpāli
summary: The questioner of the Gheraṇḍa Saṃhitā, who goes to Gheraṇḍa's hut and asks about the yoga of the pot (ghaṭastha-yoga), the cause of knowledge of reality (GS 1.1–2). The name suggests a Kāpālika.

name: Brahmānanda (author of the Jyotsnā)
summary: Author of the Jyotsnā, the standard Sanskrit commentary on the Haṭhapradīpikā. He names Meruśāstrin as the prompter of his work and reads haṭha through Pātañjala yoga and Advaita: haṭha = union of sun and moon (prāṇa and apāna); rājayoga = asamprajñāta samādhi.
notes: Not the Advaitin Gauḍa Brahmānanda Sarasvatī (tch:brahmananda-sarasvati).

name: Meruśāstrin
summary: Named in the opening verses of the Jyotsnā as the one at whose urging (abhiyoga) Brahmānanda explained the hidden sense of Gorakṣa's doctrine; the relation is usually taken as teacher and pupil.

name: Śrīnivāsa (author of the Haṭharatnāvalī)
summary: Author of the Haṭharatnāvalī, a 17th-c. manual that engages critically with the Haṭhapradīpikā (eight cleansing acts instead of six; the unity of the four yogas).
notes: Title 'mahāyogīndra' and South Indian origin are low-confidence recollections.

name: Jayatarāma
summary: Author of the Braj Bhāṣā Jogapradīpikā (1737), a vernacular haṭha compendium of eighty-four postures and twenty-four mudrās.

name: Sundaradeva
summary: A brāhmaṇa of Kāśī of the Kāśyapa gotra, son of Govindadeva and grandson of Viśvanāthadeva (colophon of the Haṭhatattvakaumudī), author of two large haṭha compendia, the Haṭhatattvakaumudī and the Haṭhasaṅketacandrikā; the colophon calls him also a physician (devavaidya, variant).

name: Bhavadeva Miśra
summary: Author of the Yuktabhavadeva (1623), which combines haṭha practice with the Pātañjala eight limbs.
notes: Distinct from the Mīmāṃsaka/Dharmaśāstra author Bhavadeva Bhaṭṭa (tch:bhavadeva-bhatta).

name: Śivānanda Sarasvatī (author of the Yogacintāmaṇi)
summary: A Daśanāmī (Sarasvatī) renouncer, pupil of Rāmacandra Sadānanda Sarasvatī (colophons), who compiled the Yogacintāmaṇi, an anthology of yoga citations with his own commentary.

name: Rāmacandra Sadānanda Sarasvatī
summary: Paramahaṃsa parivrājakācārya named in the colophons of the Yogacintāmaṇi as the guru of its author Śivānanda Sarasvatī.

name: Pūrṇānanda
summary: Bengali Śākta tantric author (Giri order) of the Śrītattvacintāmaṇi (1577), whose sixth chapter, the Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa, became the classic description of the six centres and kuṇḍalinī's ascent.

name: Kālīcaraṇa
summary: Commentator (Ṭīkā) on the Ṣaṭcakranirūpaṇa and the Pādukāpañcaka, whose commentary Arthur Avalon translated in The Serpent Power.

name: Raghuvīra (author of the Kumbhakapaddhati)
summary: Author of the Kumbhakapaddhati, a manual devoted to the kinds of breath-retention.

name: Cidghanānandanātha
summary: Name under which the Ṣaṭkarmasaṅgraha, a manual of cleansing acts, is transmitted.

name: Kapālakuruṇṭaka
summary: Name to which the Haṭhābhyāsapaddhati is ascribed in its manuscripts (recalled).

name: Mummaḍi Kṛṣṇarāja Woḍeyar III
summary: Mahārāja of Mysore under whose patronage the illustrated Śrītattvanidhi, with its section of postures, was compiled; the Mysore palace later hosted T. Krishnamacharya's yoga school under a successor.

name: Śārṅgadhara (anthologist)
summary: Compiler of the Śārṅgadhara Paddhati (1363), a verse anthology whose yoga section is an early dated witness to haṭha.
notes: Distinct from the Āyurvedic author of the Śārṅgadhara Saṃhitā.

name: Śakti (son of Vasiṣṭha)
summary: Vasiṣṭha's son, father of Parāśara, to whom Vasiṣṭha teaches yoga in the Vasiṣṭha Saṃhitā (as recalled).

name: Gārgī (in the Yoga Yājñavalkya)
summary: The woman to whom Yājñavalkya teaches the eight-limbed yoga in the Yoga Yājñavalkya; the text presents her as a learned woman (and, in some readings, as his wife). Her identity with the Upaniṣadic Gārgī Vācaknavī (tch:gargi-vacaknavi) is not settled.

name: Vāmadeva (in the Amanaska)
summary: The sage to whom Īśvara teaches the mindless yoga in the Amanaska (recalled).

name: Ādinātha
summary: U28 contribution: in the haṭha texts Ādinātha — Śiva as the first lord — is the revealer of haṭhavidyā (HYP 1.1), of the eighty-four postures (HYP 1.33), the ten mudrās (HYP 3.8, 3.128), 'a crore and a quarter' ways of laya (HYP 4.66; DYŚ 14: eight crore saṅketas), and of the Khecarīvidyā; the Jyotsnā says he taught haṭha to Girijā (Pārvatī).

name: Matsyendranātha
summary: U28 contribution: named second in the HYP's list of Mahāsiddhas (1.5), with Gorakṣa as knower of haṭhavidyā (1.4); the posture matsyendrāsana bears his name (HYP 1.26–27) and HYP 1.18 names 'Matsyendra and other yogins' as authorities on postures.

name: Gorakṣanātha
summary: U28 contribution: the haṭha texts treat Gorakṣa as the great teacher of haṭha: HYP 1.4 names him with Matsyendra; HYP 1.61 quotes 'Gorakṣa's saying' on what to avoid; HYP 4.65 credits him with the worship of the inner sound (nādopāsana) even for the dull; the Vivekamārtaṇḍa, Yogabīja and (doubtfully) the Amanaska are ascribed to him.

name: Dattātreya
summary: U28 contribution: the teacher of the Dattātreyayogaśāstra, sitting in padmāsana under a mango tree in the Naimiṣa forest when Sāṅkṛti comes to learn yoga (DYŚ 2–8); he teaches the four yogas and holds rājayoga the best.

name: Sāṅkṛti
summary: U28 contribution: the sage who wanders the earth seeking yoga and receives it from Dattātreya in the Dattātreyayogaśāstra; at the end he attains all powers by Dattātreya's grace (DYŚ 148).

name: Kapila
summary: U28 contribution: the Dattātreyayogaśāstra says 'Kapila and the others' practised haṭha (the mudrās), whereas 'Yājñavalkya and others' knew the eight-limbed yoga (DYŚ 26–27, 119); both give the same fruit.
notes: Whether this Kapila is the founder of Sāṃkhya is not stated by the text.

name: Yājñavalkya
summary: U28 contribution: the Dattātreyayogaśāstra names Yājñavalkya as the authority of the eight-limbed yoga (DYŚ 26), and the Yoga Yājñavalkya presents him teaching that yoga to Gārgī; the Jyotsnā quotes 'Yājñavalkya' on the qualifications of the yoga student.

name: Vasiṣṭha
summary: U28 contribution: the teacher of the Vasiṣṭha Saṃhitā's yoga, and named in HYP 1.18 with 'the munis' as an authority on postures (as distinct from Matsyendra and 'the yogins').

name: Śaṅkara
summary: U28 contribution: the Yogatārāvalī, a short rājayoga poem on nādānusandhāna and the mindless state, is ascribed to Śaṅkarācārya; scholars do not accept the attribution.

name: Virūpa
summary: U28 contribution: a Virūpākṣa is named among the Mahāsiddhas of HYP 1.5, and the Amṛtasiddhi is ascribed in its transmission to Virūpākṣa, commonly identified with the Buddhist mahāsiddha Virūpa; the identifications are not settled.

name: Cauraṅgīnātha
summary: U28 contribution: named among the Mahāsiddhas of HYP 1.5 (Cauraṅgī); the text says these Siddhas broke the staff of time by the power of haṭha and roam the universe (HYP 1.9).

name: Carpaṭanātha
summary: U28 contribution: named among the Mahāsiddhas of HYP 1.6 (Carpaṭi); the text says these Siddhas broke the staff of time by the power of haṭha and roam the universe (HYP 1.9).

name: Nityanātha
summary: U28 contribution: named among the Mahāsiddhas of HYP 1.7; the text says these Siddhas broke the staff of time by the power of haṭha and roam the universe (HYP 1.9).

name: Allama Prabhu
summary: U28 contribution: HYP 1.8 names 'Allama' and 'Prabhudeva' among the Mahāsiddhas — possibly the Vīraśaiva saint Allama Prabhu counted twice under two names; identification not settled; the text says these Siddhas broke the staff of time by the power of haṭha and roam the universe (HYP 1.9).
